subject: Acme RFI: outage attribution, SLO evidence, and credit mechanics
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@acme.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>; procurements@acme.com
Cc: Tom Beller <tom.beller@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: SLO measurement specifics and credit calculation

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for taking the time on the call last week. We're drafting the final RFI package for the Acme platform procurement and need a bit more depth on a few SLO/SLA points so our compliance and procurement teams can sign off. Attached is a short spreadsheet of targeted questions but the items that bubbled up after internal review are: 

- Measurement window and sampling: do you compute availability over 1m, 5m, or daily windows? How do you handle sampling for large fleets where instrumented requests vary?
- Attribution: when a request fails, how do you decide if it's customer-side, network, infra, or Redwood runtime? Any automated fault correlation?
- Time-to-detect and incident windows: what's your detection latency assumption (seconds/minutes) when bounding downtime for credits?
- Credit calculation: describe the exact numerator/denominator for service credits and whether credits are prorated hourly or by affected requests.
- Evidence for audits: what artifacts can you provide for a third-party audit (raw telemetry extracts, sampling configs, retention periods)?

Please respond with short, technical answers and any supporting artifacts you can share under NDA. We need to consolidate responses by EOD Thursday.

Regards,
Elena Park
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corp

Attachment: Acme_RFP_SLO_Questions.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@acme.com>; procurements@acme.com
Cc: Tom Beller <tom.beller@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: SLO measurement specifics and credit calculation

Thanks Elena — appreciate the clear list. I've gone through the spreadsheet and drafted concise answers below; attaching our SLO methodology PDF and a proposed credit matrix for your review. If you want a formal appendix for the RFP we can turn these into numbered clauses.

Summary answers (high level):
- Measurement windows: primary availability measurement is computed using sliding 5-minute windows sampled at request granularity, with a daily roll-up for monthly SLO reporting. We retain per-request telemetry so you can re-aggregate at 1m/5m/1h windows on request.
- Sampling: we do full-capture for transactional API keys (customers in Dedicated/Private) and dynamic sampling for hosted tenants. For hosted accounts we provide a sampled telemetry export with sampling rate metadata.
- Attribution: our routing layer annotates request traces with region, model-variant, host, and downstream infra flags. We run deterministic heuristics first (network timeout patterns, TLS handshake failures, 5xx patterns) and then optional causal inference correlators for incidents older than two minutes. Final attribution in audit exports includes a recommended cause plus confidence score.
- Time-to-detect: internal detection latency median is ~90s for service-impacting errors in our major regions (95th percentile ~6m). For contractual SLOs we use a detection window of 5 minutes by default; we can negotiate shorter windows for Dedicated capacity.
- Credit calculation: service credit is calculated as (SLO target - observed availability) * monthly invoice for the affected service, with prorating by affected customer resource groups. We calculate availability as successful responses / total served requests in the measurement window (excluded: planned maintenance and customer-induced cancellations). Credits are applied monthly and capped per the contract.

Attachments: Redwood-SLO-Methodology.pdf; Proposed-Credit-Matrix-v1.xlsx

Next steps: I can schedule a 30-min walkthrough with our SRE/product team to go through telemetry extracts and example exports. Does Wednesday 10:00 AM PT work?

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: Redwood-SLO-Methodology.pdf (methodology summary), Proposed-Credit-Matrix-v1.xlsx

Kimberly / Karthik,

Looping you in — Acme wants concrete RFI answers and artifacts. I drafted the summary replies (see thread) and attached our methodology + proposed credit matrix. Two asks before I send a final response:

1) Kimberly — can legal sign off on the proposed credit language (calculation, caps, exclusion carve-outs for customer misconfigurations)? If you have preferred clause language for the RFP appendix, please paste it in-line.

2) Karthik — can SRE confirm the detection-window numbers and whether we can guarantee a 3-minute detection window for Dedicated (for additional fee)? Also confirm what telemetry exports (format + retention) we can safely share under NDA — e.g. raw request logs for 30 days, aggregated 1m windows for 180 days, and sampling metadata.

Acme asked for a walkthrough on Wednesday; I tentatively proposed 10:00 AM PT.

Thanks — I want to keep this tight so we meet their EOD consolidation.

—D

Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI: SLO measurement specifics and credit calculation — need product/legal wording

Dylan,

Thanks for the draft. Quick responses inline below — please paste these into the RFI response and attach the methodology PDF and credit matrix. I also added a short clause you can cut-and-paste for the RFP appendix.

- Credit language (paste-ready): "Service Credits are calculated monthly as the product of the monthly invoice for the affected service and the shortfall percentage between the SLO target and observed availability, subject to the exclusions for Customer misconfigurations and scheduled maintenance. Credits will be applied as billing adjustments in the following monthly invoice and are capped at the greater of 50% of the monthly invoice or a contractual cap negotiated at signing. Customer must submit a claim within 30 days of the end of the month to be eligible for credits."

- Detection-window guarantee: We cannot guarantee a 3-minute detection SLA for Hosted customers without a Dedicated commitment and additional monitoring add-on. For Dedicated we can include a 3-minute detection window at an agreed service level (requires instrumentation agent and enhanced tracing — see line item in Proposed-Credit-Matrix-v1.xlsx).

- Telemetry export matrix: Approved exports under NDA: raw request logs (JSON, 30 days), 1m aggregated windows (CSV, 180 days), sampling metadata and config (JSON, 365 days). We will include a sanitized example export in the walkthrough.

- Audit artifacts: We can provide per-incident timelines, raw traces, sampling config, and metric rollups. All exports will be watermarked and provided under NDA. We recommend including a clause allowing Acme to request a 3rd-party auditor review once per 12 month period (costs borne by Acme).

I've attached a redline of the credit clause and a small template for an audit request procedure. Let me know when you're sending to Acme and I'll review.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Proposed-Credit-Matrix-v1.xlsx (redline stub)
